chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Yasir, from Ali ibn Ja'far al-Sakuni, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sha'iri, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:
"Whoever honored the mosque by spitting in it, Allah will meet him on the Day of Resurrection smiling, having been given his book in his right hand."

key_terms.كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ: his book in his right hand

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of spitting in the mosque according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the etiquette of *nukhah* (spitting) within the mosque, distinguishing between respectful placement and disrespect. The promise of Allah smiling and giving the book in the right hand underscores the spiritual weight of maintaining the sanctity of prayer spaces, linking physical cleanliness to ultimate divine favor.
